verified_signals.signal: Ukrgasbank ATM purchase tender UA-2026-03-20-010151-a (expected value UAH 55,264,689 incl. VAT, CPV 30120000-6) closed with contract 'EТ-19_26 Банкомати' signed to TOV 'ATM sistems' (EDRPOU 44372551) at UAH 49,720,800 - 10.03% (UAH 5,543,889) below the expected value. Scope: 36 through-the-wall ATMs + 37 lobby ATMs + 8 full-cycle lobby recyclers = 81 units, delivery by 01/12/2026, 70% prepayment within 10 banking days of signature / 30% within 10 banking days of delivery. Only two bidders: Printec Ukraine LLC (EDRPOU 35442628) at UAH 55,262,024.34 (initial = final, no price improvement) and the winner - Printec lost by UAH 5,541,224.34. Printec filed complaint UA-2026-03-20-010151-a.a1 on 17/04/2026 at 14:57 alleging the winner's equipment manufacturer had Russian-Federation links posing a national-security threat; the complaint was REJECTED and the winner's offer confirmed as the most economically advantageous. IMPORTANT PRIOR ROUND: Ukrgasbank had already run the identical 81-unit lot as UA-2025-11-20-012352-a (same UAH 55,264,689 expected value, delivery by 28/02/2026) in November 2025; that round was declared unsuccessful ('Торги не відбулися') with BOTH bids rejected for non-compliance with the tender documentation - Printec bid UAH 51,156,752.70 there, i.e. UAH 4.1m LOWER than its own March-2026 bid, while ATM sistems bid the identical UAH 49,720,800 in both rounds. The clarification thread (12 participant questions on PCI, recycler cassette configuration, heating, printers) shows Ukrgasbank refused to relax the recycler spec: it kept 'minimum 5 recycling cassettes + 1 reject/retract' (a bidder asked for 4 recycling + 1 deposit + 1 reject), kept the >=17-inch monitor (a bidder asked for 15-inch, buyer cited 'customer experience and inclusivity') and kept the >=1 serial port requirement (buyer cited compatibility with existing bank motherboards).

verified_signals.signal: NBU regulator primary, 'Кількість структурних підрозділів банків' as at 01/07/2026: Ukrainian banks operated 4,754 active structural units (branches/outlets) vs 4,815 at 01/01/2026 and 4,913 at 01/10/2025 - i.e. -61 in H1-2026 and -159 over 9 months. Oschadbank cut the most in absolute terms (1,131 -> 1,115, -16) but still runs by far the largest network at 1,115; PrivatBank 1,058 -> 1,050 (-8); Raiffeisen Bank Ukraine 292 -> 282 (-10); PUMB 219 -> 220 (+1). Separately the NBU counts 787 TEMPORARILY SUSPENDED units nationally, of which Oschadbank alone accounts for 640 (373 in Donetsk oblast, 191 in Luhansk, 27 in Kharkiv, 26 in Zaporizhzhia) - so Oschadbank's real pre-war footprint is ~1,755 units and a large occupied-territory reserve sits dormant. Oschadbank's long-run decline is steep: from 6,136 units in 2008 to 1,115 today.
verified_signals.source_name: National Bank of Ukraine - Наглядова статистика, 'Кількість структурних підрозділів банків' (Kil_pidr_2026-07-01.xlsx)
verified_signals.implies: Both target banks keep shrinking physical presence. Raiffeisen Ukraine at 282 units is materially below the ~300-306 the baseline carried, and is a country figure not to be confused with RBI group-level branch counts. Branch contraction with unchanged service obligations (Oschadbank carries a state social-payments mandate) is the classic driver for cash recyclers, assisted self-service zones and deposit automation - Printec cash automation, recyclers, self-service and managed services. Treat this as a market driver rather than a scoped deal: it sizes demand, it is not itself a procurement.
verified_signals.likelihood: Contraction has run every quarter since 2008 and continued through H1-2026; expect it to continue through 2026-2027. Next NBU data point at 01/10/2026.

verified_signals.entity: National Bank of Ukraine (open banking) - affects Oschadbank, Raiffeisen Ukraine and every Ukrainian bank
verified_signals.signal: Ukraine's open-banking regime hits its operative deadline NOW, not in 2025. The framework rests on NBU Board Resolutions No. 80 (Положення про відкритий банкінг в Україні), No. 81 (authorisation of non-financial payment service providers) and No. 82 (electronic trust services / qualified open-banking certificates), all dated 25/07/2025, sitting on top of Resolution No. 58 of 03/05/2023 (authentication and strong customer authentication on the payment market) and Resolution No. 43 of 19/05/2021 (information protection and cyber-defence for payment-market participants). THE TRIGGER: NBU Deputy Governor Oleksii Shaban stated on 26/06/2026 that practically the entire Ukrainian banking system will open its APIs in August-September 2026, with full open-banking launch in autumn 2026 and certain technical API requirements taking effect from 01/08/2026. As at 31/07/2026 the NBU register shows 6 authorisation entries - 3 PISP (payment-initiation) and 3 AISP (account-information); as at 26/06/2026 the authorised institutions were PrivatBank, PUMB and UkrSibBank (PUMB was first, in March 2026), plus two approved technology operators, Ukrainian Processing Center and TAS LINK. Every bank is an ASPSP and must, per the NBU's own published checklist: (a) run base APIs giving TPPs continuous real-time access to customer accounts, (b) publish full API technical documentation - protocols, procedures, tooling - on its own website, and (c) verify each TPP's authorisation against the Payment Infrastructure Register API plus the data in the TPP's qualified open-banking certificate before granting account access.
verified_signals.source_name: National Bank of Ukraine - Відкритий банкінг (regulator page); timing statement via Minfin/BorgExpert reporting of NBU Deputy Governor O. Shaban
verified_signals.implies: An August-September 2026 system-wide API opening is a hard, dated compliance event for Oschadbank and Raiffeisen Ukraine, not background regulation. Production-grade APIs plus mandatory strong customer authentication, consent capture/revocation, qualified-certificate handling and TPP authorisation checks create attach points for Printec digital onboarding/eKYC, transaction monitoring and fraud control, HSM/key management and AML-compliance tooling. The 'verify the TPP certificate before granting access' obligation in particular is a PKI/HSM workload every ASPSP must stand up. Approach now: banks are inside the readiness window this quarter.
verified_signals.likelihood: Technical API requirements effective 01/08/2026 (press-sourced, to be confirmed against Resolution No. 80 text); system-wide API opening August-September 2026; full launch autumn 2026; TPP volume ramping thereafter.
verified_signals.followup: Download the full text of Resolution No. 80 of 25/07/2025 from zakon.rada.gov.ua and pin the EXACT transitional dates for ASPSPs during 2026 - the 01/08/2026 date currently rests on press reporting of an NBU official, not on the resolution text. Enumerate the 6 register entries from the NBU Payment Infrastructure Register (the page's filter list is JS-driven) to confirm whether they are 6 institutions or 3 institutions holding both PISP and AISP roles. Then check whether Oschadbank and Raiffeisen Ukraine have yet published API technical documentation on their own websites - non-publication with a 01/08/2026 deadline is the opening line for a conversation.
verified_signals.verifier_note: Fetched bank.gov.ua/ua/payments/open-banking directly (WebFetch returns HTTP 403; a desktop-User-Agent curl returns 200 - logged) and read the rendered text. CONFIRMED verbatim from the regulator page: Resolutions No. 80, No. 81 and No. 82 all dated 25.07.2025 with the exact titles; the three ASPSP obligations the researcher listed (base APIs with continuous real-time access, publication of API technical documentation on the bank's own website, verification of TPP authorisation via the Payment Infrastructure Register API plus the qualified open-banking certificate); and the register counters showing 'Усі категорії 6', PISP 3, AISP 3. CORRECTED: the researcher read that as '6 authorised third-party providers'. Cross-checking against Minfin and BorgExpert of 26/06/2026, the NBU had authorised THREE institutions - PrivatBank, PUMB and UkrSibBank - so the 6 is almost certainly 6 authorisation entries across 3 institutions each holding both roles, not 6 distinct firms. Restated as register entries with the named institutions given. ADDED, and this is the most important change to the signal: the researcher gave the regime as 'live now, ramping', with a framework dated 25/07/2025 - i.e. over 12 months old, which under the standing-signal rule would have forced a [STANDING - dated 2025] tag and is_new=false. But there IS a concrete near-term trigger the researcher missed: NBU Deputy Governor Oleksii Shaban said on 26/06/2026 that practically the whole banking system opens its APIs in August-September 2026, that full launch is autumn 2026, and that certain technical requirements take effect 01/08/2026 (one day after this run). That makes the signal genuinely new and time-critical, so is_new stays true. Also added Resolution No. 58 of 03/05/2023 (SCA) and Resolution No. 43 of 19/05/2021 (cyber) from the regulator page, since they are the actual authentication and security pillars Printec products attach to. Confidence held at Medium: the regulatory core is regulator-primary but the 01/08/2026 date and the August-September window rest on press reporting of an official's statement, not on a published resolution clause. opp_size held at M.
